interface.signature: def fractionToDecimal(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> str:

preconditions.description: Both numerator and denominator are integers within the range [1, 2000].
Denominator is never zero (implicitly guaranteed by constraints).

postconditions.expression: return_value == str(numerator // denominator) if numerator % denominator == 0 else return_value
postconditions.description: If the numerator is divisible by the denominator, the output is the integer quotient as a string.

postconditions.expression: all(c in '0123456789.-()' for c in return_value) and '.' in return_value and '(' in return_value and ')' in return_value
postconditions.description: The output string contains only digits, '.', '-', '(', and ')', and includes exactly one '.' and one pair of parentheses if the decimal part is repeating.

postconditions.expression: return_value == str(numerator / denominator) if numerator % denominator != 0 and (numerator * denominator) % denominator == 0 else any('(' in return_value and ')' in return_value)
postconditions.description: If the decimal is non-terminating, the repeating part is enclosed in parentheses. Otherwise, the output is the exact decimal representation.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value.split('.')[0]) == len(str(abs(numerator // denominator))) and (return_value.split('.')[0][0] == '-' if numerator < 0 else return_value.split('.')[0][0] != '-')
postconditions.description: The integer part of the output matches the sign and absolute value of the integer quotient (numerator // denominator).
